note: Countries ISO 3166-1 lists that no curated market covers, plus the territories a job listing writes as a place of work. Each one is a generic market: its id is the lower-cased country_code, its queries name the country or one of its listed cities, and it has no curated local sources -- structured boards and Web Search reach it, a local job board does not. `cities` lists only unambiguous hubs: a city whose name is also a common US, UK or Irish place (Perth, San Jose, Valencia, Santiago, London) is left out, because a bare city name decides the market on its own. Two-letter codes are deliberately absent from aliases: a location string writes US states that way, and IN, LA, AL, ID, MD, MT and NE each name a state before they name a country. `names` gives a country or city its name per language where it differs from `name`; every one is also matched, as a whole word with accents folded, so a name that is another place or a common word in some language is left out (German Island, Spanish Granada, Japanese タイ).
